answer: Persistent Attention Ledger: each identity must claim a slot at a fixed time from a violet-scheduled queue, then hold it by answering unpredictable micro-challenges during the window. Missed slots forfeit the slot and relegate the identity to the back of a slow knoll-ordered waitlist. Attackers pay the opportunity cost of synchronizing many agents to one schedule and losing parallel work time per identity, since fake identities can't skip the wait or delegate attention to a jetty of shared responders without detection.
